item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Xi accepted open electoral contestability in the ordinary democratic sense. The closest positive evidence is only formal local participation and official propaganda about “whole-process people’s democracy,” which does not meet the threshold of free, fair, and meaningful elections.","evidence":[{"title":"On Democracy, the People Know the Best","publisher":"PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"2024-06-03","url":"https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zygy/hd/202406/t20240603_11374914.html","summary":"The ministry claimed China’s “whole-process people’s democracy” is a real democracy and said all 2.62 million deputies in the five levels of people’s congresses are elected by the people. This is the regime’s best affirmative statement, but it is a descriptive claim about participation, not proof of genuine contestability.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"Understanding China's whole-process people's democracy","publisher":"Xinhua / CPPCC","date":"2024-03-11","url":"https://en.cppcc.gov.cn/2024-03/11/c_970132.htm","summary":"Xinhua presented the two sessions as a window into “whole-process people’s democracy,” where over 5,000 legislators and CPPCC members bring proposals that later become law and policy. This shows consultative participation, not free competition for power.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"China’s democracy serves the people, safeguards development","publisher":"Xinhua / SCIO","date":"2024-07-21","url":"https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2024-07/21/content_117321904_6.htm","summary":"The SCIO said Chinese democracy includes elections, consultations, decision-making, management, and oversight, and framed reforms as advancing whole-process democracy. This is official self-justification for a nonpluralist system, not evidence of meaningful electoral contest.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"China: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House notes that independent candidates are by law allowed to run for county-level people’s congresses and that village committee elections are supposed to let residents choose representatives. This is the narrowest pro-election evidence, but the same report says candidates are often blocked by intimidation, harassment, fraud, and detention.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","3B.8"]},{"title":"China: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says there are no direct or competitive elections for national executive leaders, that the NPC’s top offices are decided in advance by CCP leadership, and that Xi’s third term means indefinite personal rule. This directly undercuts any claim of genuine electoral contestability.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"China: Freedom in the World 2026 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2026","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/china","summary":"Freedom House describes China as an authoritarian regime where the CCP tightly controls the state, media, speech, religion, universities, businesses, and civil society. It is later than the target year but confirms the same 2024 pattern: elections are not a mechanism for changing rulers.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"What to know about whole-process people's democracy in China","publisher":"Xinhua","date":"2025-03-06","url":"https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202503/06/content_WS67c8f0a0c6d0868f4e8f0784.html","summary":"Xinhua explicitly rejects “election-centric Western democratic models” and says China’s model is different, even while claiming elections are part of a broader consultation system. That is strong evidence that Xi’s system does not accept free, fair, meaningful elections as the basis of political competition.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]},{"title":"Hong Kong’s first “patriots-only” district council election cost taxpayers HK$1.2 billion","publisher":"South China Morning Post","date":"2024-04-17","url":"https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3259258/first-hong-kong-district-council-poll-after-electoral-overhaul-cost-taxpayers-hk12-billion","summary":"The article says the 2023 district council election operated under a “patriots-only” overhaul, had record-low turnout, and replaced a genuinely competitive local contest with a managed one. That is strong counterevidence that Beijing accepts contestable power.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","3B.8"]},{"title":"Press conference on guiding principles of 3rd plenary session of 20th CPC Central Committee","publisher":"Xinhua / SCIO","date":"2024-07-21","url":"https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2024-07/21/content_117321904_6.htm","summary":"The plenary guidance says reform should “advance whole-process people’s democracy” under Party leadership and strengthen institutions through which “the people run the country.” That frames elections as subordinate to Party rule, not as a means of real power contestation.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2"]}]}
